All targets are planned, with exact supplier/signature refinements and source discrepancies recorded; no proof closure or implementation is asserted.

nodes.title: Fujiwara’s minimal theorem in the Wan instance
nodes.statement: For the specified nearly ordinary weight-two residual Hilbert representation and its minimal deformation type D, identify Wan’s localized Hecke algebra with the R=T algebra supplied by R21.4. Verify every condition of Fujiwara 11.1, then use 11.2 and 11.5 for freeness of the precise quaternionic/Hilbert module and the Hida-family comparison. The minimal algebra is a relative complete intersection; the appropriate finite flat Hecke algebra is Gorenstein. This is an application of the supplier theorem, not a new proof of totally real R=T.
hypotheses: p>3; F totally real, p unramified in F; residual representation absolutely irreducible on G_{F(ζ_p)}.
For p=5 exclude the simultaneous PGL2(F5) projective-image and mod-p-cyclotomic factorization through its abelianization of order two.
The local nearly ordinary types are distinguished; flat types satisfy Fujiwara’s unramified base-field restriction; a minimal modular lift exists as in Definition 6.11.

Verify Hypothesis 6.7 via Theorem 6.8 in the ordinary/weight-two instance; retain Hypothesis 5.9 in exactly the nonminimal cases where 11.1 requires it. Odd [F:Q] requires the Shimura-curve Ihara input in Wan 8.

Exclude the actual exceptional 0E case using the induced-representation description: the local representation is absolutely irreducible, its inertia restriction is absolutely reducible, and q_v≡−1 mod p. BCS H3 excludes this case. Additionally verify Wan 8’s literally printed irreducible-inertia q_v test. SourceIssues E1/E5 explain the wording discrepancy; the literal test alone is not used as an exclusion of the actual induced type.
proofSteps: Match the determinant, Teichmuller twist characters, finite local deformations away p and nearly ordinary/flat local deformation conditions, not just residual representations.
Apply the exact minimal supplier theorem and freeness; the existing nice-prime Skinner–Wiles theorem in R21.4 is not by itself this theorem.
Use finite flatness over the regular weight ring and complete-intersection duality to deduce Gorenstein; finite flatness alone does not imply regularity.

nodes.statement: In the imported ordinary GU(2,2)/F module of p-adic forms, take the Klingen family ℰ_D supplied by APL L4 from the actual local sections and pullback, and prove its normalized coefficient and boundary identities. nodes.title: Wan’s coefficient Eisenstein ideal
nodes.statement: For Λ_D→h_D, where h_D is the reduced localized cuspidal ordinary Hecke image, let J index the exact characteristic-polynomial coefficients, central-character values and ordinary U_p eigenvalues in Wan §9.1. For every unramified inert place include all coefficients of Q_v−Q_v,D and its central Z_v,0 difference; for each split place include Q_w−Q_w,D, Q_wbar−Q_wbar,D and both central Z_v,0^(i) differences. Use i_w=1 and i_wbar=2: Q_w uses T_i^(i_w) with the complementary central operator Z_0^(3−i_w), and Q_wbar uses T_i^(i_wbar) with Z_0^(3−i_wbar). Correct the repeated i_w in the printed second polynomial as recorded in E6. The polynomial constant coefficient is 1, so only degrees 1–4 contribute. At every v|p include u_t,v−λ_ℰ_D(u_t,v) for t=diag(p^a1,p^a2,p^a4,p^a3), a1≤a2≤a3≤a4. Reciprocity uses geometric Frobenius and the central character is σ_ψσ_ξ^−1. Write H_j∈h_D and λ_j∈Λ_D for these cuspidal operators and Eisenstein values. Let I_D be the ideal generated by H_j−λ_j, and define 𝔈_D=I_D∩Λ_D, equivalently the kernel of Λ_D→h_D/I_D. The exact Hecke-generator dictionary proves the structure map onto h_D/I_D is surjective, so Λ_D/𝔈_D≅h_D/I_D. The definition does not assume surjectivity or identify a reducibility ideal with a congruence ideal.
hypotheses: The coefficient inclusion is a unital ring map; the Hecke carrier, reduced image and eigenvalues are supplied by the ordinary-form/IHG owners.
The actual index set J contains all operators listed in Wan §9.1, with its central and U_p relations.

nodes.title: Cuspidal lift and Eisenstein congruence length
nodes.statement: At a height-one prime P of Λ_D not pulled back from R+, with a nonconstant Fourier coefficient of ℰ_D outside P, construct a cusp family congruent to ℰ_D modulo the Rankin factor L^Σ. After localizing the source at P, the induced Λ_D,P-algebra map (h_D/I_D)⊗_ΛD Λ_D,P→Λ_D,P/(L^Σ) is onto. The separate global coefficient map Λ_D→h_D/I_D is onto by the Hecke-generator dictionary. Its kernel 𝔈_D satisfies ord_P(𝔈_D)≥ord_P(L^Σ). In the rational projector variant retain b e_f integral, b(φ0)≠0, P⊂φ0, and the coefficient nonvanishing condition on b times the rational family.
hypotheses: The integral family and coprimality theorem, ordinary boundary exact sequence and lifting/control theorem hold for all cusps.
P is height one; the local ring is a DVR; the Rankin factor is nonzero. The unwanted abelian factor is removed only with the actual unit/localization argument of Wan.
proofSteps: Use Wan 27 to lift the cuspidal reduction of the family; verify the boundary and flatness hypotheses of the form module.

In the localized cusp module, evaluate a Hecke translate at a coefficient invertible at P. Divide by that coefficient to obtain a Λ_D,P-linear functional. The congruent eigenvalue relations modulo P^r prove multiplicativity and unit preservation on the Hecke quotient; linearity alone does not make a ring map.

The localized quotient map gives 𝔈_D Λ_D,P⊂P^r Λ_D,P, with r=ord_P(L^Σ). Use source-specific Gorenstein duality only where required, and keep the coefficient/global quotient distinct from its localization.

nodes.title: Polarized 1+2+1 extension with ordinary local conditions
nodes.statement: Import integral determinant/reconstruction ingredients from IHG, and apply the exact polarized rank-four three-block extension theorem of Wan Proposition 98 as a recorded supplier refinement to the actual cuspidal rank-four Galois representation congruent to χ′⊕ρ⊕χ. Verify all ten hypotheses of Wan §9.2.1 on the completed height-one Hecke algebra. The resulting extension classes belong to the Σ-imprimitive ordinary Selmer group for the same rank-two lattice and twist as the Rankin function. For P0⊂I[[Γ_M]] height one not pulled back from R+=I[[Γ_M+]], require that P=P0Λ_D is the corresponding height-one prime. If the plus/minus local constituents are residually disjoint modulo P, obtain ord_P0(char X^Σ)≥ord_P(𝔈_D).
hypotheses: Λ_D is a Krull domain; h_D is finite, local and reduced. The selected localized/completed congruence model satisfies the coefficient-intersection and quotient clauses of Wan §9.2.1; these clauses require proof and do not follow merely from finite flatness.
The three residual constituents are disjoint, the rank-two one absolutely irreducible, and the polarization and local ordinary characteristic polynomials have Wan’s twists.

The cuspidal characteristic-zero constituents are absolutely irreducible or satisfy the precise rank-two alternative in condition (10); CAP exclusion and ordinary modularity lifting prove this alternative.
The scalar-character Selmer characteristic ideal has valuation zero at P by the totally real character main conjecture; the plus/minus local pieces have no common irreducible constituent modulo P.

For primes containing 𝔈_D, use A=completion of (Λ_D)_P, a DVR, and the corresponding completed Hecke factor R. Choose the source model A0,R0,I0,J0 so I0∩A0=J0, A0/J0≅R0/I0 and the extended ideals contract as required by Wan §9.2.1. Global I_D,𝔈_D do not automatically contract unchanged after height-one localization. A supplier may use their P-primary saturations only after proving the same local quotient lengths and valuations. At a prime not containing 𝔈_D the congruence valuation is zero.

Wan setup (1)–(3): use H=G_F,Σ, G=G_M,Σ and its conjugation c. The continuous polarization character ν extends to H; χ is a continuous character of G and χ′=νχ^(−c) has different residual character. The rank-two ρ is defined on a free A0-lattice, satisfies ρ^c≅ρ^∨⊗ν, and its residual representation is absolutely irreducible and disjoint from both residual characters. Residual disjointness is witnessed by coprime characteristic polynomials of some group-algebra element, as in the supplier theorem.

Wan setup (4)–(6): the rank-four σ is defined over the image of R0 in R, with integral traces and a finitely generated R-orbit module for every vector. It satisfies the same polarization; the proper congruence ideal I has nonzero J=A∩I and A/J≅R/I, and tr σ≡χ′+tr ρ+χ modulo I. The irreducible ρ has a compatible polarization pairing Φ with Φ^t=−ν(c)Φ.

Wan setup (7)–(9): at every v|p the plus and minus rank-two lattice pieces are free over A0, and the plus and minus rank-four pieces are free over R⊗_A Frac(A). For every element x of the local group algebra, the plus characteristic polynomial of σ agrees modulo I with Ch(ρ^+,x,T)(1−χ(x)T); the minus relation uses χ′. The two combined local pieces have no common residual irreducible constituent.

Wan setup (10): for each characteristic-zero specialization of R⊗_A Frac(A), σ is absolutely irreducible or has the specified absolutely irreducible rank-two subrepresentation whose trace is congruent to χ+χ′. The ordinary lifting and CAP exclusion supplier proves this alternative; it is not assumed for an arbitrary trace.

Match the exact twist dictionary of Wan §9.2.2, p.87: ρ=ρ_f⊗σ_ξ^(−c)σ_ψ^c ε^(−2), χ=σ_ψ^c ε^(−3), and χ′=νχ^(−c), using ε for the p-adic cyclotomic character. The final Selmer lattice is (T_f⊗I[[Γ_M]])(ε_M^(−c))⊗ε and its ordinary line, with the actual coefficient map and primitive/Σ conventions. All height-one extension and coefficient normalization comparisons are verified before identifying the valuations.

Characteristic valuations use the divisorial height-one-length construction over the normal coefficient ring, with faithful localized/completed scalar transport; principality is not inferred from normality.
proofSteps: Use IHG determinant/Hecke algebra ingredients. The current upstream IHG.6 statement concerns rank-two representations with two residual characters; it is not Wan’s rank-four χ′⊕ρ⊕χ theorem. Request that exact general extension input without replanning the existing rank-two theorem, and use the AC L0 bridge for its ordinary Selmer realization.

nodes.title: Wan’s parallel Hilbert-family divisibility
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real of degree d, p≥5 unramified in F, M/F CM with p split, and I a local normal finite integral extension of the parallel Hida weight algebra.
